Build a Type-Stratified Sampled Edge List for Non-Spatial scRNA Data

Source: R/create_Edgelist_SamplingByType.R
create_Edgelist_SamplingByType.Rd

Constructs a directed edge list for non-spatial single-cell communication analysis by randomly sampling cell pairs within each ordered cell type crossing. For every directed type pair (A -> B), the function:

  1. Computes a per-crossing cap: min(n_A, n_B) (further bounded by max.cells if supplied).

  2. Independently samples cap cell barcodes from type A (senders) and cap barcodes from type B (receivers) without replacement.

  3. Pairs them positionally – the k-th sampled sender is paired with the k-th sampled receiver.

All T^2 directed crossings are covered, including autocrine (A -> A), where both sender and receiver are sampled from the same type.

Important: Individual edges are biologically synthetic – the specific cell pairing within a type crossing is arbitrary. Only aggregate signals across all edges of a given type pair carry biological meaning. Results differ across runs unless seed is fixed.

Usage

create_Edgelist_SamplingByType(
  meta.data,
  cell.type.col,
  seed = 42L,
  max.cells = NULL
)

Arguments

meta.data

data.frame with one row per cell. Row names must be unique cell barcodes. Must contain the column specified by cell.type.col.

cell.type.col

character(1). Name of the column in meta.data that holds cell type labels.

seed

integer(1). Random seed for reproducibility. Default 42L. Pass a different value to obtain an alternative sampling draw; pass NULL to skip seed-setting (not recommended for publication). The caller's random number state is restored on exit.

max.cells

integer(1) or NULL. Optional upper cap on the number of edges per type-pair crossing. When NULL (default), the cap is min(n_i, n_j) for each crossing. When set, the cap becomes min(n_i, n_j, max.cells), preventing very large types from producing an excessive number of edges even when paired with another large type.

Value

A data.table keyed on (from, to) with columns:

from

Sending cell barcode (character).

to

Receiving cell barcode (character).

Carries metadata attributes: mode ("nonspatial"), param (named list of cell.type.col, seed, max.cells), n.cells (total cells in meta.data), cell.names (all cell barcodes).

Details

This function is a low-level primitive: it builds the sampled non-spatial edge list that create_NICHESObject consumes internally when called with mode = "nonspatial". Most users should call create_NICHESObject(mode = "nonspatial", ...), which invokes this function and assembles the result into a full NICHESObject in one step. create_Edgelist_SamplingByType() is exposed for power users who want to inspect the sampled edges, fix the random seed explicitly outside the wrapper, or feed the edges into a custom scoring pipeline.

Cell types with zero cells after barcode-matrix intersection are silently skipped. Type crossings where the effective cap is zero (e.g., one type has no cells after filtering) are also silently skipped.

See also

create_NICHESObject, create_Edgelist_Spatial

Examples

set.seed(1)
meta <- data.frame(
  cell.type = sample(c("ATI", "gCap", "Macro"), 300, replace = TRUE),
  row.names = paste0("cell_", 1:300)
)
el <- create_Edgelist_SamplingByType(meta, cell.type.col = "cell.type",
                                     seed = 42L, max.cells = 50L)
#> [create_Edgelist_SamplingByType] 3 cell types | seed = 42 | max.cells = 50 | 450 sampled directed edges.
